tool.name: ERA5 / ERA5-Land Climate Data Extractor
tool.description: Download daily ERA5 / ERA5-Land climate data via Open-Meteo
tool.command:
python '$__tool_directory__/era5_extractor.py'
## ── Coordinate file ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── --coordinates '$coord_file'
## ── Climate variables (multi-select produces space-separated tokens) ───────── --parameters #for $p in $parameters '$p' #end for
## ── Date range ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #if $dates.mode == 'global' --start-date '$dates.start_date' --end-date '$dates.end_date' #end if
## ── Coordinate reference system ───────────────────────────────────────────── --epsg $epsg
## ── Output ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── --output-format '$output_format' --output '$output_file'
## ── Advanced: API key (paid tier — optional) ───────────────────────────────── #if $advanced.apikey.strip() --apikey '$advanced.apikey' #end if
## ── Advanced: sleep between requests ───────────────────────────────────────── --sleep $advanced.sleep

param.name: coord_file
param.label: Coordinate file
param.help: CSV or TSV with one row per site. Must contain EITHER 'latitude' + 'longitude' columns (decimal degrees in the CRS given by the EPSG code below) OR a 'geometry' column with WKT strings (POINT, LINESTRING, POLYGON …). For non-POINT geometries, all of the available points will be used in the API query. Optional columns: 'site_name' (row label used in the output); 'begin_date' and 'end_date' (YYYY-MM-DD) for per-site date overrides.

param.name: parameters
param.label: Climate variables to download
param.help: Select one or more daily variables. ERA5-Land variables (soil moisture, soil temperature, mean 2 m temperature) are automatically routed to the ERA5-Land sub-model; all other variables use ERA5. Results for all variables are merged on the date column.

param.name: mode
param.label: Date range source
param.help: Global: same start/end dates applied to every site. Per-site: dates are read from 'begin_date' and 'end_date' columns in the coordinate file (no global dates needed).
param.option: Global dates — same period for all sites
Per-site dates — from coordinate file columns

param.name: start_date
param.label: Start date
param.help: Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Earliest allowed: 1960-01-01 (SAFRAN lower bound). Overridden per row by a 'begin_date' column in the coordinate file.

validator.message: Date must be in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 1990-01-01).

param.name: end_date
param.label: End date
param.help: Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Latest allowed: 2020-12-31 (SAFRAN upper bound). Overridden per row by an 'end_date' column in the coordinate file.

validator.message: Date must be in YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g. 2020-12-31).

param.name: epsg
param.label: Input coordinate EPSG code
param.help: EPSG code of the CRS used in the coordinate file (default: 4326 = WGS-84 geographic, decimal degrees). Coordinates are automatically reprojected to WGS-84 before the API call; the output always stores WGS-84 lat/lon. Examples: 2154 (RGF93/Lambert-93 France), 32631 (WGS84/UTM zone 31N), 3035 (ETRS89/LAEA Europe).

param.name: output_format
param.label: Output file format
param.help: CSV and TSV are human-readable. JSON is useful for downstream web applications. Parquet is a compact columnar binary format suitable for large datasets (requires pyarrow).

param.name: apikey
param.label: Open-Meteo API key (paid tier — optional)
param.help: Leave empty to use the free tier (archive-api.open-meteo.com), limited to 10 000 requests/day per IP address.

param.name: sleep
param.label: Sleep between API calls (seconds)
param.help: Minimum pause between successive HTTP calls (default: 1.0 s). The free tier allows at most 600 requests/min, 5000/hour, 10000/day. Increase this value if you receive repeated HTTP 429 errors. Set to 0 only when using the paid API key.

tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**ERA5 / ERA5-Land Climate Data Extractor** downloads daily climate and soil data from the ERA5 and ERA5-Land reanalysis datasets via the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (https://open-meteo.com). No Copernicus account or API key is required for the free tier.
-----
What it does ============
For each location in the coordinate file and each selected climate variable, the tool queries the Open-Meteo archive API and assembles a single output table with **one row per site per day**.
The extraction period is bounded by SAFRAN data availability: **1960-01-01** (earliest) to **2020-12-31** (latest).
-----
Coordinate file format ======================
A CSV or TSV file with **one row per site**. Must contain one of:
- ``latitude`` + ``longitude`` — decimal degrees in the CRS given by the *EPSG code* parameter (default: WGS-84). - ``geometry`` — WKT string (POINT, LINESTRING, POLYGON, …); any CRS, reprojected automatically. For non-POINT geometries the **centroid** is used.
Optional columns:
- ``site_name`` — label in the output and logs (default: row_N). - ``begin_date`` / ``end_date`` — per-site date range (YYYY-MM-DD) that overrides the global start/end dates for that row.
**Example — simple POINT sites (WGS-84)**::
site_name,latitude,longitude Montpellier,43.611,3.877 Paris,48.857,2.352 Bordeaux,44.838,-0.579
**Example — per-site date ranges**::
site_name,latitude,longitude,begin_date,end_date Ultuna,59.817,17.655,1970-01-01,2018-12-31 Pergamino,-33.920,-60.560,1985-01-01,2015-12-31
**Example — polygon geometry (WGS-84)**::
site_name,geometry Bassin_Herault,"POLYGON((3.5 43.4,3.9 43.4,3.9 43.8,3.5 43.8,3.5 43.4))"
-----
Smart model routing ===================
Variables are automatically split between ERA5 and ERA5-Land sub-calls and merged on the date column:
- **ERA5-Land** (~9 km, land only): mean 2 m temperature, soil moisture, soil temperature. - **ERA5** (~25 km, global): precipitation, ET0, wind, radiation, humidity, pressure.
This avoids the silent empty-response bug that occurs when ERA5-Land variables are requested directly from the seamless endpoint.
-----
API quota and Galaxy deployment ================================
The **free tier** is limited to **10 000 requests per day per IP address**.
When the free quota is hit, the script automatically pauses until midnight UTC (when the quota resets) and resumes — the job does **not** fail.
-----
Output columns ==============
- ``site_name`` — from the coordinate file (or row_N if absent). - ``site_id`` — numeric identifier, one per extracted point (1, 2, 3, …). - ``latitude``, ``longitude`` — WGS-84 decimal degrees of the queried point. - ``date`` — ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD). - One column per requested climate variable.
